== Biography ==

The Nome King, also known as King Roquat or Roquat, rules an underground cavern beyond the Land of Ev, at the head of the Nomes. His standing in the world is defined largely by his enmity with Ozma and her allies: Ozma once marched with Dorothy and her army to his cavern and forced him to liberate the captives he held there, who belonged to the Royal Family of Ev. During that same encounter, the Scarecrow nearly frightened the Nome King into fits by throwing one of Billina's eggs at him, and Dorothy captured his Magic Belt, carrying it away to the Land of Oz.

According to the Tin Woodman, the Nome King "has not a kind heart" and has harbored wicked thoughts of revenge ever since his defeat and the loss of the Magic Belt. In response, he has ordered his Nomes to dig a long tunnel beneath the desert so that he may march his hosts directly into the Emerald City.

== Narrative role ==

The scheme against Oz surfaces when Ozma studies the Magic Picture and [[Tin Woodman]] tells the travelers what she has seen there: Nome King has had his subjects dig a tunnel beneath the desert so he can march an invading host into the Emerald City, joined in the plot by the Whimsies, the Growleywogs, and the Phanfasms. The invasion collapses through Scarecrow's countermeasure — dust stirred up inside the tunnel leaves the marching army parched, and when the thirsty host drinks from the Forbidden Fountain the water strips them of their hostility; Nome King alone resists drinking, so he is thrown bodily into the fountain as well, and Ozma sends the rest of the disarmed army home again using the Magic Belt.

== Personality ==

The Nome King is vengeful: after his defeat and the loss of his Magic Belt, the Tin Woodman describes him as harboring "wicked thoughts of revenge." The Tin Woodman further characterizes him as lacking kindness, stating flatly that "the Nome King has not a kind heart."

Despite his menace, he shows real fear: the Scarecrow once "nearly frightened the Nome King into fits" merely by throwing one of Billina's eggs at him. The same skittishness resurfaces in the company of his most powerful allies, the Chief of the Whimsies and the Grand Gallipoot of the Growleywogs, before whom he "seemed a bit fearful."

Yet in directing his own war plans he is calm and decisive, answering without hesitation that a march begun at midnight would bring his combined army to the Emerald City "by daybreak."

== Appearance ==

The Nome King is referred to as the old monarch, ruling from his underground cavern beyond the Land of Ev.

== Powers ==

The Nome King's rule was for a time backed by a Magic Belt, a magical item he possessed as King Roquat. Dorothy captured this Magic Belt during the campaign that freed the captive Royal Family of Ev and carried it away with her to the Land of Oz, stripping the Nome King of the artifact.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Ozma]]''' — enemy. Ozma once marched with Dorothy's army to the Nome King's underground cavern and forced him to liberate his captives, an episode that seems to mark the two as adversaries.

'''[[General Guph]]''' — employment. Guph stood beside the Nome King as one of his generals, and the king's remark "I'm sorry I did not make you my General before" suggests an employment bond between them.

'''[[Dorothy]]''' — enemy. Dorothy captured King Roquat's Magic Belt and carried it away to the Land of Oz, an act that suggests lasting enmity between the two.

'''[[Scarecrow]]''' — enemy. The Scarecrow reportedly frightened the Nome King into fits by throwing one of Billina's eggs at him, which suggests an antagonistic relationship.

'''[[Grand Gallipoot]]''' — wary_alliance. The Grand Gallipoot's words "Don't let us quarrel now, friends. First let us conquer Oz" could indicate a cautious alliance with the Nome King, tempered by underlying tension.
